effect: Approval becomes loss-averse and elections see busts. Growth above the world rate adds +1.5 approval per point (was +5.4); growth below it costs -3 x min(Tb, 1.2) per point, at most -3.6 (was -1.8 x Tb; Tb is the game's 0.4-1.8 grievance factor, which still scales the other economic terms in full). Losses weigh 2x gains at the typical factor 1 and 2.4x at 1.2 or more; in the few countries whose grievance factor is below 1 (as low as 0.4) busts weigh less, as the game intends. Real approval and vote shares move about 1-2 points per point of growth, with losses weighted about 1.5-2x gains (realism check 2026-10-30; mod 0.1.0 used +2.5 and -3.5 x Tb, up to -6.3 per point, and produced approval gaps of up to 38 points in a one-year run). Elections: during the first year the input is as in the original game (booms only), because day-0 growth is partly seeded from observed data and decays toward the model's own rate (finding A4). From day 365 the daily society tick re-takes the reference growth gap once (_growthGap0, an existing saved field; the day it was re-taken is stored as geobalGrowthRef365, so a save already past day 365 gets it on its first day with the mod); from then on the input is the signed gap to that reference, floored at -3 points (booms unbounded, as in the original). In the party-choice model the ruling-party multiplier is 1 + 0.08 x gap for booms (unchanged) and max(0.5, 1 + 0.12 x gap) for busts. Day 0 unchanged: approval is re-anchored at genesis (_apprAnchor) and the election gap is 0 by construction. (Minified names in this text are those of build 26296134; the patch's find text has the current ones.)
